preconditions.description: The number of cities n is between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(p_list) == n - 1 and all(1 <= x < i for i, x in enumerate(p_list, start=2))
preconditions.description: The parent list contains n-1 integers where the i-th element (1-indexed relative to cities 2..n) is strictly less than i, defining a valid tree structure rooted at 1.
The number of bus routes m is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for a, b in routes)
preconditions.description: Each bus route connects two distinct cities within the valid range [1, n].
The number of queries q is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= v <= n and 1 <= u <= n and v != u for v, u in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query asks for a path between two distinct cities within the valid range [1, n].

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q lines, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all((int(line) == -1) or (int(line) >= 1) for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is either -1 (indicating no path) or a positive integer representing the minimum number of buses.

postconditions.expression: all((int(output_lines[i]) == -1) == (not reachable(v, u, routes, tree)) or (int(output_lines[i]) == min_buses(v, u, routes, tree)) for i, (v, u) in enumerate(queries))
postconditions.description: For each query (v, u), if v and u are not connected via any sequence of bus routes, the output is -1; otherwise, the output is the minimum number of bus routes required to travel from v to u, where a single bus route covers the unique simple path between its endpoints in the tree.
